title: everydeck app map 1.12-r0: the exact technical analysis of an app (facts with evidence, nothing judged)

function_ref.description: a function is name + file; refer to it by its name, or as <path>#<name> when the name is not unique

via.description: element data only: how the frontend reaches the table: from, table, collection, doc, realtime postgres_changes, sql, rpc <function>, function <edge function>, view <view>, route <pattern> (the route whose handler reads the table), model <class>

shown.description: a display location: where the app shows a table, column or status (element = the UI element with the visible text), or (element "data") where the frontend reads the table (supabase.from(x), a Firestore collection, an ORM query in a page or component, or a call of an API route whose handler reads x); a table with any display location belongs to the main navigation; the generator writes element data from the syntax tree (TypeScript compiler API, Python ast) and names the access path in via

value_labels.description: the text the app shows for a value of this column, from a mapping in the code (an object keyed by the value, a switch, an i18n key built from the value, <option value> under a <select> bound to the column); the place is the text itself (the line in the code or in the translation file); lang is the language of the translation file (file or folder name); without such a mapping the value has no label and stays as it is

updated.description: the database sets this column on every change (a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that sets NEW.column = now() or moddatetime(column), SQLAlchemy onupdate=func.now()); the read scope uses it as the change column for changed_since; the place is the trigger or the model column

written.description: places where the app changes this column after the record exists (supabase .update/.upsert, UPDATE … SET, updateDoc, Prisma update data, a database function that writes a parameter); everydeck lets the owner edit only columns the app itself changes

contact.description: the column holds contact data or a message of a person: email (an e-mail address), phone (a phone or messenger number), ip (an IP address), message (a text one person writes to another or to the operators). The place is where the app itself treats the value that way: a link mailto:/tel:/sms:/https://wa.me/, an input of type email or tel, the place that writes the request IP, the form where a person writes the message. Columns of type inet/cidr are IP addresses by their type. everydeck never reads such a column in its read scope; the approval lists it under "Only you see".

production_in_code.description: the address or key of a production service written into the code (database URL and key, error-tracking DSN, …), a fact with its place; everydeck shows the owner a hint

icon.description: the icon the app itself serves (link rel icon / apple-touch-icon in an HTML entry, web manifest icons, Next.js app/icon.*, Expo expo.icon) with the place that names it; data = the file in base64 (at most 96 KiB). everydeck keeps a copy for the app card and never stores the data in the app map.

described.description: what the page is for, as facts: the tables the page shows or edits (each with a place in works_with or a display location) and the flows that start on it; empty lists = the page shows no records and starts no flow. Written by the coding agent for a new page; everydeck asks for it as an order.

name_rule.description: how the app builds the name of a person from columns of the identity table, as the app shows it: steps in order (the first with content wins, a fallback), each step the columns joined with the separator of the app (first and last name); evidence = the places that show it; the generator writes it from the code, nothing is guessed; everydeck uses exactly this rule

auth_table.description: the user table of the login provider when it is outside the app schema (Supabase: auth.users); a foreign key or a policy comparison (auth.uid() = column) to it is a reference to the identity; fk.table may name it

shown.description: display locations of the table (list, heading) and (element data) every data access of the frontend; up to 60

schema.description: schema of the table when it is not the default (public); the read scope names the table as schema.name

not_shown.description: only for a table without any display location: every place where a frontend source file names the table in a string (a write such as from(…).insert(…), a write request to a route, a label or key, a module no screen imports) with the fact (what the place is) that makes it no display; everydeck-check's independent cross-check refuses a table without display location whose name appears in the frontend without such an entry

role.description: the role string as the code checks it, or a list when the code accepts several roles

source.description: ES1: the signal is sent from browser code with the browser SDK (everydeck.signal(name, ctx.operationId)); without it only a server key may send it

purpose.description: the flow is the app's sign-up, sign-in, password reset or payment: these are always flows when the app has them (flow_candidates with required); verification: the identity check of a person by a provider (e.g. Didit), never required

everydeck_tables.description: tables the everydeck installation added to the app (outbox, operator links, the request log of the app bridge) with the place that creates them: everydeck's own, never objects of the app; also tables in everydeck's schemas (everydeck_outbox, everydeck_read, everydeck_bridge) and tables defined in the file of an everydeck adapter

display_ends.description: places where the app shows a value as an image, link, textarea, text with line breaks or date, but the value cannot be followed back to a column; the fact says where the path ends (a call of a function, a property that is no column, a fixed value); the generator writes it, nothing is guessed

unreachable.description: frontend files no entry of the app reaches through imports (entries from facts of the project: <script src> of an HTML file, route files of a framework the package.json names, package.json main): no page, no display location; the generator writes it, everydeck-check checks it with the same rule

works_with.description: what the users of the app work with: the things they see, create or edit in the UI; one entry per table with the place in the UI (page or component, file:line); part_of names the table whose detail page shows it (CVs with the candidate, members with the workspace) and gets no menu item of its own. This list is the main navigation; every other table is under 'All data'. A description with evidence, no judgement: everydeck-check checks that the place exists and names the table (or carries a display location of the table)

flow_candidates.description: written by the scaffold: every write of the browser to a table or an API route, every trigger of the app, every place the app signs people up or in, resets a password, opens a checkout or receives a payment webhook. Each one is a flow of the app map (result.write on its table, its place as the start, or the purpose) or carries left_out with the reason; required ones cannot be left out. EV1: left_out is a note and keeps the candidate open and visible; close it with outcomes[] (covered_by a flow that explains it, or not_applicable with a place)

redirect.description: password_reset with Supabase Auth: the page of the app for a new password (redirectTo in the code), a path only

way.description: CV2: one of several ways of the same kind (id <kind>@<way>): the sign-in method (password, code, oauth, sso, otherwise the method), or the file of a write or checkout; only a flow on this way (its start or result at this place) explains it

money.description: the payment provider with the places where the app talks to it, and the tables with money, each with its place (the scaffold writes what it finds, the agent adds tables without a provider with a reason); everydeck reads amounts only from the app's own data, never from the provider

reason.description: because described_by_agent: what in the code shows that the table holds money (e.g. the price list the upgrade form reads, the plan an admin grants after a bank transfer)

holds.description: what a row is: a plan or subscription that runs for a period (plans), a one-off purchase such as an order, a ticket, a boost or a credit pack (purchases), a request to buy that waits for payment (requests), or the app's own price list (prices)

roles.description: columns of this table by their meaning for money; each must be a column of the table

currency.description: the one currency the code uses for this table (e.g. a formatter or a column name with the code), when no column holds it

minor_unit.description: the amounts are stored in the smallest unit of the currency (cents), with the place that shows it (e.g. division by 100, Stripe unit_amount)

statuses.description: what a value of the status (or of roles.period's table status column) means for money, each with the place in the code

price.description: the amount is not in this table but in the app's own price list: roles.product names the row of the price list by its key column; amounts per period (the period comes from roles.period)

log.description: CV2: the table only logs events (for example the stored webhook events of the provider): no row is a plan, a purchase, a request or a price, so it has no holds; with the place where the app writes or reads it as a log. An entry with neither holds (and the columns that carry money) nor log keeps the money part open

ai_calls.description: written by the scaffold: AI clients and calls of the app (provider, place, the model where the code names it); everydeck counts numbers only, never prompts or answers

outcomes.description: EV1: the outcome of each open part everydeck found (ids from everydeck-check validate, field open[].id). covered_by: the flow that explains this concrete operation; not_applicable: why it does not apply, with a place in the code that shows it. Both close the part. deferred and unsupported keep it open and visible to the owner; a text such as 'later' never closes anything. covered_by may name further parts in also (ids from open[], each listed explicitly) that the same flow explains in exactly the same way, for example the same report sent from several pages; parts not listed stay open

also.description: Further ids this covered_by answers, each listed (never all parts of a kind silently)

inventory.description: EV1: written by everydeck-check validate --repo (do not edit): what everydeck-check found in the repo itself, with the version of the tool, the commit and a digest; everydeck compares it with the app map

not_checked.description: CV2: files that may carry a schedule everydeck-check does not read (another host's file that names one, or a known file it cannot read); schedules set only in a dashboard are not in the repo

way.description: CV2: one of several ways of the same kind (id <kind>@<way>): the sign-in method (password, code, oauth, sso, otherwise the method), or the file of a write or checkout; only a flow on this way (its start or result at this place) explains it

used.description: EVX: a money table only: the first place where the code reads or writes it (path:line), found the same way validate refuses a not_applicable

schedules.description: CV2: planned work found without a package: pg_cron in SQL (cron.schedule), crons in vercel.json, cron services in render.yaml, the schedule of a GitHub Actions workflow; each is an open part until a jobs[] entry at its place describes it
